name: Visto per lavoro autonomo (self-employment visa, Decreto Flussi quota)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a qualifying self-employed, professional, or entrepreneurial activity, with prior authorisation or professional registration where the activity requires it under Italian law.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the intended activity is a recognised self-employment category and secure any required professional authorisation.

requirements.blocker_text: Competes for one of only 650 national self-employment quota slots for 2026, within the same Click Day mechanism as subordinate work -- one of the tightest quotas of any route category found across this dataset.
requirements.fix_path: File during the Click Day window and expect very high competition for the limited slots.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires investment of at least EUR 500,000 in an activity of interest to the Italian economy and the creation of at least 3 new jobs -- a dedicated 500-of-650 sub-allocation within the annual self-employment quota. This specific sub-allocation figure rests on a single specialist legal-consultancy source rather than a directly-fetched government page confirming the exact split, unlike the general self-employment quota mechanism above.
requirements.fix_path: Structure a qualifying investment of at least EUR 500,000 with at least 3 new hires.

evidence_required.document: Proof of financial resources adequate to the activity
Professional registration or authorisation, where the activity requires it

sources.title: Prefettura della Spezia (prefettura.interno.gov.it, Ministero dell'Interno field office) -- Decreto flussi 2026-2028, confirming D.P.C.M. 2 ottobre 2025 (Gazzetta Ufficiale 15 ottobre 2025) Art. 5's 164,850-unit total quota and Art. 6's subordinate/self-employment sub-allocation

Studio Legale Avvocato Francesco Lombardini -- Decreto Flussi 2026-2028: quote, click day e nulla osta, detailing the 650/year self-employment quota breakdown including the investor-entrepreneur and Venezuela-descendant sub-allocations

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING, one of the tightest single-category quotas found anywhere in this dataset: only 650 self-employment slots exist nationally for the whole of 2026, compared to 76,200 subordinate-work slots in the same Decreto Flussi cycle -- a roughly 117-to-1 ratio favouring employer-sponsored over independent work, a far starker imbalance than any other country's work_sponsored-vs-work_independent split documented in this build. Within that already-tiny 650, 500 slots are specifically reserved for the EUR 500,000-plus investor-entrepreneur sub-category (modeled here as its own OR-logic group, since it carries a materially different, higher-bar qualifying test than the general self-employment slots), leaving only about 150 slots nationally for all other self-employment categories combined. A genuinely distinctive detail found only in this route across the entire dataset: a dedicated 50-per-year sub-allocation exists specifically for descendants of Italian citizens (up to the 3rd degree) legally resident in Venezuela or other MAECI-designated countries -- an ancestry-linked quota carve-out inside an otherwise ordinary economic-migration channel, distinct from and smaller in scope than it_ancestry_jure_sanguinis's own separate citizenship-recognition route, but worth flagging as a related, narrower benefit for a subset of the same population. This mirrors a broader pattern documented elsewhere in this dataset (Saudi Arabia's Karta-Polaka-adjacent quota nuances, China's overseas-Chinese PR track) of ancestry functioning as a narrow accelerant embedded within an otherwise unrelated route category, rather than only appearing as its own standalone ancestry-category route. selection_odds.approx_rate_percent is left null rather than guessed, since no source gave a defensible applicant-to-slot ratio -- only the raw slot counts, which are reported instead in the basis field.
